title: Lungs
summary: The lungs are the body's air-exchange organs - soft spongy sacs that bring in oxygen and let out carbon dioxide. Explore the branching airways and the tiny air sacs where gas exchange happens.

compareCandidate.label: Lungs vs. gills
compareCandidate.description: Lungs are internal air sacs that take oxygen from the air; fish gills are feathery structures that take oxygen dissolved in water. Both perform gas exchange, but in very different environments.

processes: Exchanging oxygen and carbon dioxide in the alveoli
plainLanguageExplanation: The lungs are two soft, spongy organs inside the chest. When you breathe in, air travels down your windpipe and divides into branching tubes (bronchi and bronchioles) that end in millions of tiny clusters of air sacs called alveoli. The alveoli are wrapped in a network of tiny blood vessels, and it is here that oxygen crosses into the blood and carbon dioxide crosses out to be breathed away. The lungs are covered by a smooth membrane and are protected by the ribcage. The right lung has three lobes and the left lung has two, because the heart sits on the left side.

whyItMatters: The lungs keep every cell in your body supplied with oxygen and clear it of carbon dioxide. Understanding them explains why you breathe faster during exercise, why smoking is harmful, and how the respiratory system works.
didYouKnow: Your lungs together contain around 480 million alveoli - if spread out flat they would cover an area about the size of a tennis court.
